title: Strong clarinetists: Pills, Jimbo and George Lewis
summary: He liked Pills, found Jimbo timid, does not remember George Lewis from then, and notes the men who left town.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well I guess you're about the strongest clarinet player they have left, I am, Neely. Who in the old days was strong like that? Big tone.

Well, what I could say, I liked Pills. He was a pretty good clarinet player. I liked Pills very well. Now Jim was a good clarinet player. Jimbo, you understand? But Jimbo had a whole lot of chicken in him. Yeah. He was ready to run in to see somebody got noise, he couldn't fly. He'd done a couple of times, I'd run him off the truck just by going around him. Just by going there and looking at him playing. Got off the truck, got a man, take a walk. And they saw him home, took one day, went home, got my clarinet, and I jumped on the truck in each place. And you see me there. You take Pills, Zed, George. Those men play it. Good clarinet player. Chazel. Chazel. I liked the card, that's a good friend of mine. Which George is this?
Georgey Boy. Oh, Georgey Boy. There's so many George's. How about George Lewis in those days? Do you remember him?

Well George, George was alright. George Lewis was alright. But I didn't know George in, let's see. I was up in there in that time doing Jimbo. Doing Jimbo and Zep and them. I don't remember George at all.
Well he's eight years younger than George. He wouldn't be around now. I guess by the time he got to going, Jimbo had left town.

Well I guess that's about it. Yeah, that's about it. Because I don't remember him. I know, I know, I know probably all the musicians, man. But I was down through here and most anywhere around in two, three hundred miles. A little more. All the men when they left. Jimbo, Jimmy Collar, all them big men. Orin, Oliver and all that bunch when they left. Lewis.
